Linter runs in under 1 second on any text output

beats.role_note: the stakes BEFORE the build begins — no terminal yet
beats.narration_text: An AI system writes a progress report. It says the model achieves eighty-three percent coverage — a number that sounds authoritative and is not cited anywhere. It uses the word 'demonstrates' three times. Every sentence with an unsourced number is a claim that could be fabricated. Every over-warranted verb is evidence that outruns its data. The linter catches both before a human reads the report — and the --strict flag makes it a gate that blocks the commit.
beats.visual_intent: title card: 'the unsourced 83% — a claim that looks like a fact'; PROBLEM beat, no terminal yet

props.command: the unsourced 83% — a claim that looks like a fact

beats.narration_text: In the terminal: ask Claude to write a Python script that reads a markdown file and flags two things. First: any sentence with a digit or percent sign and no adjacent citation marker — print as UNSOURCED NUMBER. Second: any sentence using proves, demonstrates, shows, or conclusively without a linked figure or table — print as OVER-WARRANTED VERB and suggest the licensed downgrade. Print line numbers and a summary count.

props.command:
claude "Write a Python script that reads a markdown
file and flags:
(1) sentences with a digit or % and no citation
    marker ([n], (source), or 'per <file>') —
    print as UNSOURCED NUMBER
(2) sentences with proves/demonstrates/shows/
    conclusively and no linked figure/table —
    print as OVER-WARRANTED VERB + suggest downgrade
Print line numbers + summary count."

beats.role_note: terminal (Onda) — read the output before running
beats.narration_text: Read the two regexes before running. UNSOURCED NUMBER matches any digit or percent sign and checks for the absence of a citation marker nearby. OVER-WARRANTED VERB matches the four verbs from the chapter's taxonomy — proves, demonstrates, shows, conclusively — and checks for the absence of a figure or table reference. The taxonomy is the point: hypothesize, suggest, observe, find, show, demonstrate, conclude, prove — each one further out on the evidentiary limb.

props.title: output_linter.py

beats.role_note: screen-recording — linter flags real lines in a draft report
beats.narration_text: Run it on a real report draft. Seven flagged lines. Three say 'UNSOURCED NUMBER' — sentences with percentages and no citation. Two say 'OVER-WARRANTED VERB' — 'demonstrates' and 'shows' without a linked figure. One is a false positive: a year in a section header. The linter is not perfect, but the five real flags are five sentences that would have shipped as fabricated claims without it.
beats.visual_intent: screen-recording: linter running on report.md, 7 flagged lines printing with line numbers and categories, summary count at bottom

props.title: terminal: python output_linter.py report.md
props.code:
$ python output_linter.py report.md

L12 UNSOURCED NUMBER: The model achieves 83% coverage.
L28 UNSOURCED NUMBER: Error rate dropped to 4.2%.
L31 OVER-WARRANTED VERB: This demonstrates robustness...
L44 UNSOURCED NUMBER: Only 17% of records were flagged.
L67 OVER-WARRANTED VERB: The results show that Claude...
L89 UNSOURCED NUMBER: Accuracy improved by 11 points.

(L55: '2024' in header — possible false positive)

Summary: 5 UNSOURCED NUMBER, 2 OVER-WARRANTED VERB, 7 total

beats.narration_text: Add a --strict flag that exits with code one if any unsourced number is found, then wire it as a pre-commit hook so a report with a fabricated number cannot be committed. Ask Claude to write both the flag and the hook snippet. The linter stops being a suggestion the author might ignore and becomes a step that blocks the commit.

props.command:
claude "Update output_linter.py:
add --strict flag: exit code 1 if any
UNSOURCED NUMBER found. Add a pre-commit hook
snippet that runs output_linter.py --strict on
any staged .md file — blocks commit if it fails
with: 'Report contains unsourced numbers.'"

beats.narration_text: The verified-data contract is enforceable, not just aspirational. Unsourced numbers and over-warranted verbs are the two shapes fabrication takes — and both match a regex. The --strict flag makes the linter a gate: a report that can't be committed until its numbers trace is a report that has to be honest. The verb taxonomy is the chapter's contribution: hypothesize, suggest, observe, find, show, demonstrate, conclude, prove. Each one further out on the evidentiary limb than the linter will let you go without a figure behind it.
beats.visual_intent: recap card: 'UNSOURCED NUMBER + OVER-WARRANTED VERB = the two shapes fabrication takes'; verb taxonomy scale

beats.narration_text: Your move: run this linter on the last progress report you wrote. Count the UNSOURCED NUMBER flags. For each one, either add a citation marker pointing to the real record, or delete the number. Both moves are honest. Replacing the number with a citation is better; deleting a fabricated claim is still better than leaving it.
